1000131.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Sotho Lesotho (“land of the Basotho (Sotho people)”). The immediate transmission route into Norwegian is unknown.
The Sotho name belongs to a characteristic noun-class pattern based on Sotho: Mosotho (“a Sotho person”), Basotho (“Sotho people”), Sesotho (“Sotho language”) and Lesotho (“land of the Basotho”).
Parallel international adaptations include Norwegian Nynorsk Lesotho, Afrikaans Lesotho, Swedish Lesotho, German Lesotho, Dutch Lesotho and English Lesotho.

The last part øy, from Old Norse ey (“island”), from Proto-Germanic *awjō (“floodplain, island”), from earlier *agwjō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ékʷeh₂ (“water”). Doublet of Karlsøya.

1004995.etyen:
PIE word
 *werdʰom
Compound of kort (“short”) + verb (“verb”), literally “short verb”.
The first element, kort (“short”), is ultimately from Latin curtus (“short”), from Proto-Italic *kortos, ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *(s)ker- (“to cut off, sever”). The second element, verb (“verb”), is borrowed from Latin verbum (“word; verb”), from Proto-Italic *werβom (“word”), from Proto-Indo-European *werdʰom (“word”), ultimately from the root *werh₁- (“to speak, say”).
Compare the parallel formation Norwegian Nynorsk kortverb (“short verb”).
